title: Top K Frequent Elements
followUps: Compare the complexity of sorting all counts, using a size-k heap, and bucket sort. When would you choose each?
How would you compute the top k over a stream of elements that never ends?
How would you compute an approximate top k across logs spread over thousands of machines?
How does your solution behave if k equals the number of distinct elements?

interviewer.approach: Count with a hash map (O(n)). Then either sort by count O(u log u), keep a min-heap of size k O(u log k), or bucket sort by frequency O(n). Bucket sort is the optimal answer; a heap is a strong answer. Quickselect is O(u) average.
hints: Start by figuring out how often each element appears. What structure makes that easy?
Once you have counts, do you need to fully sort them to get the top k? What structure keeps only the k best?
Frequencies are bounded by n. Could you index buckets by frequency instead of sorting?
pitfalls: Using a max-heap over all elements (O(u log u)) and claiming O(n log k).
Off-by-one in bucket sizes (frequency can equal n).
